feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: WNBA star Nneka Ogwumike has earned a little rest
entry.summary: Nneka Ogwumike's legacy was never in question winning a championship and league MVP within four years. Negotiating the largest collective bargaining agreement in pro sports for the WNBA ensures it.

entry.title: To train robots, AI companies are paying people in India to film themselves doing chores
entry.summary: Men and women across India are being paid to record themselves doing domestic jobs as developers train AI robots to do household chores.

entry.title: This week in science: sea monsters, long COVID patients' microbiome, elephant carcasses
entry.summary: NPR's science podcast Short Wave brings us stories about the hunting habits of ancient sea monsters, the microbiome of long COVID patients, and how elephant carcasses replenish the savannah.

entry.title: The planned public execution has been canceled, but what message did it send?
entry.summary: President Trump announced that the Fort Hood attacker's execution will not be livestreamed. NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with New Yorker journalist Dexter Filkins, who witnessed a public execution.

entry.title: Three years on, Israel still bars foreign journalists from entering Gaza
entry.summary: More than a year into a declared ceasefire in Gaza — and three years into the war — Israel still hasn't allowed foreign media independent access to Gaza.

entry.title: Actor and author Nick Offerman reflects on a place that shaped him
entry.summary: On Wild Card, well-known guests answer the kinds of questions we often think about but don't talk about. Actor and author Nick Offerman reflects on a place that shaped him.

entry.title: When students learn to 'Speak,' they also learn to listen
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Jennifer Tiexiera and Mfaz Mohamed Ali, filmmaker and original oratory competitor, about their documentary, Speak, and the importance of speech clubs in schools.

entry.title: After holding 'The Italian Job,' reporter welcomes Italy's pull
entry.summary: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly talks with Jason Horowitz about his memoir, The Italian Job, and his years spent learning the ropes in Rome and reporting on Italy's biggest stories.

entry.title: Hit a midlife wall? Here's how to rediscover your strengths
entry.summary: Health and science correspondent Allison Aubrey talks with Ailsa Chang about her new podcast Your Turn with Allison Aubrey — and they share a survey that can help us identify our most positive character traits.

entry.title: Minnesota's plan to keep elections safe from federal interference
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon about how his state is preparing for the upcoming midterm elections.
